acceptance: A request to any of the 98 /api route files whose Host is not a literal loopback authority, whose Origin is not http(s)://<Host>, or whose Sec-Fetch-Site is not absent, same-origin or none gets 403 {"error":"Same-host requests only"} from server.js before Next is invoked (all route classes: public read, private read, form write, JSON write, delete, credential, multiplayer, e2e hook).

The same rule judges every WebSocket upgrade (multiplayer socket, HMR path, any other) before the path or bearer is read: a foreign Origin or rebinding Host gets 403; a same-host client still reaches the existing bearer check.

Encoded, doubled-slash, dot-segment, backslash, upper-case, absolute-form and undecodable spellings of /api are guarded, and an API prefix that Next routes by (for example /api/pilots/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e, a dynamic-route parameter that decodes to separators or dot segments) can never be erased by normalising later parameter content; page routes are not guarded (ruling 7).
Requests with no Origin and no Fetch Metadata are still served (same-host controls).

The rule lives once in src/lib/api/sameHostGuard.ts; local-seats, token and unlock call it first, before the method check, the handlers' Zod parseBody, rate limit and KDF; the custom server guard precedes Next's HTTP parsing, but under bare next dev (dev:e2e, already disclosed as bypassing server.js) Next's own body parser runs first. local-seats behaviour and error text are unchanged and its existing suite passes unchanged.
server.js exits 1 at boot when tsx or the guard cannot load; a failure after boot answers an API request 500 and destroys an upgrade, never admitting either unguarded (ruling 2).
The one WebSocketServer refuses an inbound frame larger than 1 MiB: exactly 1,048,576 bytes accepted and 1,048,577 closed with 1009 on the match and campaign channels.

scripts/validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs exports assertSameHostGuard and main() calls it on the built, unflagged server (rebinding-Host read 403, cross-site form 403 with no identity created, the encoded dynamic-route target /api/pilots/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e 403 for a foreign Host and not 403 for the loopback Host, a page route not 403 for a foreign Host, same-host read 200, foreign-Origin upgrade 403). Not wired into CI here (DESKTOP-GUARDS-1).
No session, cookie, rate-limit or error-text change; extraction preserves local-seats behaviour.

limitations: Fatal boot (ruling 2): if tsx or the guard cannot load, server.js logs "[mp-boot] same-host guard unavailable" and exits 1 before it prints the ready marker. In the packaged app the embedded-server wrapper rejects with "The embedded server exited before it was ready (code 1, signal null)" (desktop/electron/main.server.ts:39) and the window shows the Startup Error dialog "MekStation could not start its local server." with Retry and Quit (desktop/electron/main.window.ts:281-298). Retry restarts the server; with a permanently missing tsx or guard the dialog returns on every attempt, and Quit closes the app. Until now only the guard-free multiplayer runtime load was non-fatal (server.js:540 logs "[mp-boot] runtime load failed" and keeps serving Next without multiplayer); the guard is the first thing that makes tsx fatal for the whole app.

Later load failure (ruling 2): loadSameHostGuard() caches a successful load, so only a failure inside the guard call can happen after boot. An HTTP request then reaches the existing catch and is answered 500 "Internal Server Error", never handed to Next; an upgrade reaches the existing catch and the socket is destroyed without a handshake (no 500 status line, no 101). Both are rows of the candidate test.

Page routes and _next assets (ruling 7): a DNS-rebinding page can still read HTML pages and _next assets (rebinding reads of pages are not judged). Only /api and upgrades are. Every upgrade is judged, including the dev HMR path.

dev:e2e (next dev --webpack) bypasses server.js: that lane has the guard only on the three credential routes (local-seats, multiplayer/auth/token, vault/identity/unlock). No workflow or script uses it (package.json, a comment in scripts/qc/run-flow-audit.mjs, a test fixture).

Requests with no Origin and no Fetch Metadata (Electron main, curl, Node, Playwright request) stay admitted (owner decision 2026-10-25 item 8): a local process can still call the API; the guard stops browser-mediated attacks only.

The packaged validator is a manual gate until DESKTOP-GUARDS-1 (ruling 8). Its main() call of assertSameHostGuard is exercised only by a packaged run (survivor-by-construction, not a mutant); the non-vacuity rows prove the checker itself against fake servers.

Server-entry rows run the real server.js, real ws and real tsx with next, the multiplayer runtime modules and SQLite stubbed by a Module._load preload (technique of validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.test.ts). Real Next dev (HMR, compile of a refused route), Playwright, the hydrated image and the packaged Electron run are NOT proven here; the e2e-smoke CI job is the only proof of real Next dev. The corrected F1 refusal is additionally proven on an actual built, unflagged image (builtNextProbe), as scratch candidate evidence; the exact-merge Jest rows themselves remain stubbed.

The 1 MiB cap is a product decision, not a measured margin: CampaignProposal.proposal is z.unknown on the wire schema and nothing on the server bounds it below the cap. maxPayload limits received messages only; outbound snapshots and replay chunks are not affected.
Node's own fetch and WebSocket send no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site (probed on Node 24.15 in the prep refresh, not re-run on 22.22 here); the frozen L1 harness requests are plain loopback.

S7-09 (unthrottled vault sign route), S5-06 and B15-AUTH-LIMIT stay outside this unit. No session, cookie, rate-limit or error-text redesign. B15-AUTH-ORIGIN is absorbed by annotation; B15-1 keeps its operator session scope.
On Windows a raw HTTP upgrade client with the default keep-alive agent loses every second refusal to ECONNRESET; the candidate tests use agent:false. Test hazard, not a product bug.

Body parsing (precise): the custom server guard precedes Next's HTTP body parsing and the three direct credential guards precede the handlers' Zod parseBody, rate limit and KDF; under bare next dev / dev:e2e Next's own body parser runs before any handler, so pre-HTTP-parser refusal is not claimed there.

Over-guarding is conservative and unchanged in kind: a page target whose parameter decodes to an /api path (for example /compendium/equipment/..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Fapi) and a literal /api/../x are judged API and refused for a foreign Host (185 such page-control targets, the same count under the previous guard in the differential; the literal /api/../x form is new in kind but unroutable by browsers).

The F1 diagnostics prove classifier disagreement and that API handlers were reachable; they do not prove data extraction or a successful write, and none is claimed. Next's matcher is an upper bound: real Next served the home page for /api/replay-library/%2e%2e/%2e%2e.

correctionF1.trigger: Both independent reviews of e975d71ef95234d08a88b38199b69a55c6779022 (review-sol-e975d71ef.md, review-opus-e975d71ef.md) returned REQUEST-CHANGES for the same defect; Root ruled F1 blocking and authorized this correction (carry-forward.md "Root ruling: #2371 both reviews REQUEST-CHANGES").
correctionF1.defect: The frozen guard decoded the target up to three times and only then resolved dot segments, so `/api/pilots/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e` collapsed to `/` and was judged a page while Next matched it as `/api/pilots/[id]` and decoded the id to `../..` afterwards. A foreign Host and Origin were admitted past the boundary for 47 dynamic API routes.
correctionF1.claimsNotMade: The diagnostics prove classifier disagreement and that the API handler code path is reached; no data exfiltration and no successful write is claimed. Neither review executed a write. The pre-fix built probe reached the handlers, which answered "Pilot ../.. not found", "Share link not found" and "Version 1 not found".
correctionF1.fix: isApiRequestTarget in the single owner is now true if EITHER reading says API: the existing fully decoded and collapsed reading, or a second reading of the raw target that Next routes by (leadsWithApiSegment): backslashes normalised, split on literal slashes only (an encoded %2F or %5C stays inside its segment), no dot-segment resolution (Next does not resolve %2e), first non-empty segment decoded up to three times and compared case-insensitively with `api`. Parameter content can no longer undo a recognised prefix. No new dependency, no eleventh leaf, no rule weakened, pages not guarded to hide the bug.
correctionF1.designNote: A first version of the second reading resolved real and %2e dot segments (the reviewers' WHATWG suggestion). The Next-matcher differential showed 4 remaining misses (`/api/replay-library/%2e%2e/%2e%2e`: Next matches the raw segments as parameters, it does not resolve %2e) and the arm was simplified to the pure raw-prefix reading before any test or freeze. Neither reviewer algorithm was copied.

builtNextProbe.purpose: Authorized and required: the correction against an actual built, unflagged Next image with the raw target on the wire. Scratch candidate evidence; not a merged-source mainProof, an RC acceptance or a replacement for the later implementation proof.
